chunks: Fadala and al-Qasim from Kulaib al-Asadi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who owns his parents and his brothers, so he said: 'If he owns the two parents, they have been freed; but he may own his brothers, so they remain slaves and are not freed.'
ai.seo_question: Does owning one's parents or siblings automatically free them from slavery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal mechanics of manumission (*itq*) within family structures, establishing that owning one's parents automatically triggers their emancipation due to the inherent dignity of parenthood, while siblings may remain enslaved if not explicitly freed. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic view that the parent-child bond carries a specific legal weight that precludes permanent servitude, whereas sibling relationships do not inherently confer the same automatic status of freedom upon ownership. The ruling underscores the principle that *itq* is an active legal act that can be instantaneous through ownership in the case of parents, reflecting the high status of parents in Islamic law.
